findings.claim: The landmark_00_local_dx coordinate proxy is non-monotone across the full observed support [0.0,0.49]: it rises from near zero to a positive peak around t≈0.10-0.11, reverses to a deep negative trough around t≈0.18-0.20, then recovers toward slightly positive values by t≈0.49. The whole-window mean is near zero (whole_window_z≈-0.18), so the net displacement over the window is small relative to the within-window excursion.

The endpoint rates are strongly signed and opposite: first_rate_z≈-17.5 and last_rate_z≈+8.1, with 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches. This indicates the direction of change is not stable within the window and that batch-level sign agreement is weak, so a single monotone trend should not be assumed.

A degree-2 polynomial fit was not accepted (polynomial_accepted=false) and relative node RMSE is high (≈0.78), so the observed curve is not well described by a smooth low-order global trend; the contrast is dominated by mid-window structure rather than a stationary target.

The learning/control support is [0.0,0.5] with 50 observed score nodes at 0.01 spacing, and label semantics are recorded affinities removed with an equal score prior; extrapolation beyond the observed support is not allowed.

hypotheses.direction: unchanged control geometry; treat the contrast as non-monotone with a mid-window reversal
hypotheses.falsifier: A re-read of the same curve over the same support showing a monotone trend with no sign reversal, or a stable low-order polynomial fit with relative node RMSE below the reported value.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx curve over observed score nodes [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.scope: whole observed window [0.0,0.49], all 50 score nodes
hypotheses.statement: For the landmark_00_local_dx coordinate proxy, the observed contrast is a mid-window reversal rather than a monotone drift: positive excursion early (peak near t≈0.10-0.11) followed by a negative trough (near t≈0.18-0.20) and partial recovery. Any temporal dose policy should be evaluated against this non-monotone shape rather than assuming a single direction of coordinate change.

hypotheses.direction: defer a directional dose change; require batch-stable sign agreement before assigning a time-dependent direction
hypotheses.falsifier: Batch-resolved rates showing consistent sign across independent batches with no strong sign conflicts.
hypotheses.observable: first_rate_z, last_rate_z, sign_changes, strong_sign_conflicts, independent_batches for landmark_00_local_dx
hypotheses.statement: Because first_rate_z and last_rate_z have opposite signs with 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches, the endpoint rate direction is not a reliable guide to a single temporal dose direction; a timing benefit cannot be distinguished from batch-dependent sign instability using this proxy alone.

limitations: Only one coordinate proxy (landmark_00_local_dx) was read; other landmark coordinates and soft_mass features were not queried, so cross-feature consistency is unobserved.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; no stage boundary or discovered phase is claimed.
Descendant survival and decoded final affinity are not observed in this role input, so selection preference is treated as association only, not as measured final benefit.
The curve is a coordinate proxy in predicted endpoint world coordinates; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is attached.
Unqueried evidence is not unavailable evidence; additional features may show different or contradictory temporal structure.
